title: Potatoes
ingredients: One Potato, Two Potato, Three Potato, Four…
directions: In a big bowl or roasting pan or rimed baking sheet, combine all the ingredients and toss.
Spread the potatoes in a single layer for roasting.

Roast, tossing with a spatula a few times to prevent sticking, until the potatoes are very tender throughout and the skins are somewhat shriveled and crisp, around 50 minutes, depending on their size and variety.
Clean and dry the potatoes. Then pierce them in a few spots with a fork or sharp knife to allow steam to escape (and prevent an explosion!).
For a softer skin, you can roll the potatoes in some olive oil or butter, then maybe roll the potatoes in some crunchy salt.
Put the potatoes in the oven to cook until done, about 45 minutes.
Serve hot with you favorite toppings, such as butter or sour cream or chives.
You can also bake the potatoes at 350 degrees for 60 minutes if that’s a better use of your oven.

If you’re in a hurry, you can microwave the cleaned, dried, and punctured potatoes for about 20 minutes first; then bake for about 10 minutes in the hot oven to make the skin crisp. (Use less microwave time if you have less than 4 potatoes.)
Sweet potatoes are also delicious just baked, but may not need as much time as regular potatoes (around 10 minutes less).
Clean and dry the potatoes. Then pierce them in a few spots with a fork or sharp knife to allow steam to escape (and prevent an explosion!).
Put them in the oven to cook until done, about 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon over medium high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble and set aside.
When potatoes are done allow them to cool for 10 minutes. Slice potatoes in half lengthwise and scoop the flesh into a large bowl, being careful not to tear skins; set potato skins aside.
To the potato flesh add sour cream, milk, butter, salt, pepper, 1/2 cup cheese and half the onions. Mix until well blended and creamy.
Spoon the mixture into the potato skins. Top each with remaining cheese, green onions and bacon.
Bake for another 15 minutes and serves hot.

Sweet potatoes (yams, really) are also delicious with just a simple roasting (i.e. without all the butter, brown sugar, and marshmallows that you sometimes see at Thanksgiving). The thyme and garlic combination goes especially well.
